question: What is the primary goal of aseptic techniques during immunization?
explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed to stop harmful microbes from contaminating sterile items and entering the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: Why are injections considered high-risk procedures for infection transmission?
explanation: Breaking the skin destroys the body's first line of defense, allowing any surface microbes on contaminated tools to enter deep tissues directly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h1)

question: When should an alcohol-based hand rub be used instead of soap and water?

options.A: When hands have visible dirt on them
options.B: Before eating lunch in the ward
options.D: When hands are not visibly soiled

explanation: Alcohol rubs work quickly to kill germs on clean skin, but physical dirt requires the friction of soap and water to wash away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: A nurse wears clean gloves to vaccinate an infant. Is hand hygiene still necessary?

options.A: Yes, hand hygiene must happen before and after glove use
options.B: Only if the gloves tear during the procedure
options.C: No, gloves completely eliminate the need for hand washing
options.D: Only if the mother requests hand washing

explanation: Gloves can have microscopic holes or become contaminated during removal, making hand hygiene mandatory every single time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: What must always be used to reconstitute a lyophilized vaccine?

options.A: Normal sterile saline from any available brand

explanation: Using the exact diluent provided ensures correct chemical balance and prevents contamination or vaccine inactivation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: A nurse notices a vaccine has exceeded its recommended storage temperature range. What is the best action?

options.A: Administer it only to adult clients
options.B: Use the vaccine quickly before it degrades further
options.C: Consult policy guidelines before discarding the affected vials
options.D: Place it back in the freezer to restore potency

explanation: Heat-damaged vaccines lose their potency and fail to protect the client, requiring proper verification and safe disposal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h3)

question: Why must the alcohol swabbed on a skin site dry completely before injection?

options.A: To ensure the cotton swab sticks better
options.B: To prevent the alcohol from stinging the patient
options.C: To allow the chemical to fully kill surface bacteria
options.D: To make the skin easier to puncture

explanation: Disinfectants need adequate contact time to destroy microbes; injecting through wet alcohol causes burning and reduces antiseptic action. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: What happens if an injection site is massaged vigorously after administering certain vaccines?

options.A: It can cause local irritation or rapid drug absorption
options.B: It helps the vaccine spread evenly through the bones
options.C: It stops any potential bleeding instantly
options.D: It speeds up the growth of protective antibodies

explanation: Massaging can alter how the body absorbs the antigen, sometimes increasing local tissue reactions and discomfort. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: What practice is strictly forbidden immediately after administering an injection to prevent injury?
explanation: Trying to recap a used needle with two hands frequently results in accidental stabs to the fingers and hands. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: When should a sharps safety box be sealed and replaced?

options.A: After ten needles have been dropped inside
options.B: Only at the end of every calendar month
options.C: When every single side is completely bulging
options.D: When it reaches the specified fill line

explanation: Overfilling a sharps box increases the risk of protruding needles piercing staff during handling or transport. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h5)

question: Which color container is universally used for infectious medical waste like blood-stained cotton?
explanation: Yellow bins and bags are standard for infectious and hazardous healthcare waste requiring specialized treatment like incineration. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to throw empty glass vaccine vials into ordinary household trash bins?

options.A: It increases the cost of municipal waste trucks
options.B: Government inspectors check household bins daily
options.C: Scavengers or waste sorters could be cut or exposed
options.D: The glass will react chemically with food waste

explanation: Discarding medical items in regular trash exposes members of the community to injury and residual biological hazards. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h6)
